checks: Read the report entry and work summary; round-1 fixes (physical priors, dof-corrected significance, Habun vs Hexc/Hcol discussion, Occam/error-model sensitivity over 42 combos, profile likelihood of the equal-A contrast) are all done and the '2.5-3 sigma' wording is withdrawn.

Recomputed p-values from the quoted dchi2 and dof: 7.7/3dof p=0.053 (1.9 sigma); 5.0/2dof p=0.082 (1.7 sigma); 6.7/2dof p=0.035 (2.1 sigma); 12.7/3dof p=0.005 (2.8 sigma). All agree with the report. One small slip: 'doubled errors dchi2 3.5, p=0.3, 1 sigma' is p=0.17 (1.4 sigma) for 2 dof (p=0.32 only for 1 dof); this does not change the conclusion.

Agree that the physical-prior rerun removes the grid-edge (n=1e3, kpc path length) branch and that the answer is robust: excitation/opacity alone reaches a contrast of about 1.1-1.3 against an observed 1.45-1.50, so abundance (or per-nucleus 12C/13C) is favoured at roughly 2 sigma, not excluded either way. Confidence 'low' and the hedged Habun-vs-Hexc wording are appropriate.

Consequences are derived: N(HCN)/N(HCO+) of 3.2 (N) and 2.0 (S), a ~60% HCN enhancement, the X_S>=130 alternative branch, and discriminating predictions for 13C/12C ratios of HNC, CO and HCO+ (equal N/S for abundance, S lower for 12C/13C). I did not re-run the RADEX grids; I checked internal consistency of the numbers and statistics only.
notes_for_questioner: (1) The question quotes 1.48 (1-0) and 1.85 (3-2), but the matched 2.2" analysis gives 1.45 and 1.50. The 3-2 value of 1.85 is probably a smaller-beam or peak-pixel value; state the beam dependence explicitly in any write-up (the contrast rises at smaller beams, consistent with the compact HCN-rich core at N) and consider a two-component core+envelope model. (2) Decisive follow-ups: deep H13CN at S, HN13C/HNC and 13CO/C18O in matched beams, and an independent Tk (CH3OH, H2CO). (3) Fix the p=0.3 / 1 sigma quote to p=0.17 / 1.4 sigma in the doubled-error case.
